set.body:
# C0 platform-trace diagnostic worker task

## Authority and scope

Create a clean worktree at
`/private/tmp/scalafim-execution-20260929/c0-platform-trace` from base
`16f7e35b`. The parent will create the Mote child under original PHRF-21
`bd-01M25Q0JY8GA7CJRKZF2934PJ0`; use actor `exec-diagnostics`. Do not edit,
claim, or reserve paths before the parent has created that child. The worker is
not alone. No recursive agents, dashboard, source-scope expansion, publication,
or whole-cohort work.

Own **exactly** these four paths:

1. `modules/first-level-laws/shared/src/test/scala/scalafim/fmri/laws/profile/ConditionC0QualificationSuite.scala`
2. `modules/first-level-laws/shared/src/test/scala/scalafim/fmri/laws/profile/ConditionC0PlatformTraceSuite.scala` (new)
3. `modules/first-level-laws/shared/src/test/scala/scalafim/fmri/laws/profile/ConditionC0LiteralFixture.scala` (new)
4. `docs/verification/condition-c0-platform-trace-2026-09-30.md` (new)

Do not edit `ShapeDecoder.scala`, `CompactCondition.scala`, build files, runtime
platform shims, public APIs, or the frozen C0 policy. No full C0 study, direct
oracle grid, reseed, tolerance change, budget change, or scientific-gate work
is authorized.

## Fixed specimen

The only numerical specimen is the candidate-policy C0 input identified by the
completed frozen study:

- source freeze `451be51b9abca9c127c9d8d2f012d7ef871f262922ec5c68ae3f7f06513e023d`
- development SNR `.5`, seed `102`, voxel `120`
- `ConditionC0QualificationHarness.Candidate` unchanged: 6 Newton steps, 12
  jets, 2 exact evaluations, 8 candidate attempts per iteration (total upper bound 13), stationarity tolerance
  `1e-9`.

`ConditionC0LiteralFixture.scala` contains exactly 600 raw IEEE-754 `Long`
bits for the **already whitened, selected-response column**, captured once from
that frozen specimen. It exposes a fresh `Array[Double]` by
`java.lang.Double.longBitsToDouble`; it must not call `Random`, convolution,
whitening, directCohort, the direct oracle, or any decoder. Validate count,
finite values, and a fixed fixture digest in the suite. Record the complete
literal source hash and digest in the verification document.

The factory added to `ConditionC0QualificationSuite.scala` is test-only and
package-visible. It returns a fresh diagnostic setup using the existing frozen
`preparation`, the literal column, candidate budget, normalisation
`Unnormalised`, no prior, and noise variance `1.0`. It may project the literal
column using `CompactConditionPreparation.project`, then point a fresh
`CompactConditionObjective`; it must not invoke `directCohort`, `runStudy`,
`referenceCohort`, or `CompactConditionRuntime.fit` as an input generator.
The public fixture must be independent of platform RNG behavior.

## One-time response-only capture

The frozen receipts do not contain raw input bits. Before final literal tests, use a bounded temporary JVM-only capture entry inside the owned test scope to execute the EXISTING frozen directCohort(200, .5, 102) response generator, whiten the responses exactly as the frozen study did, and export ONLY column120's 600 raw Long bits. Generating the response arrays is authorized; calling any decoder/reference/oracle/cohort study is not. Capture once, retain its complete raw/meta evidence plus source/prerequisite/fixture identity, then hardcode those bits in the literal file. The final diagnostic factory and literal tests consume only the hardcoded column and never invoke this capture path. A retained opt-in capture helper may have a dedicated explicit property and no ordinary test activation; avoid changing normal harness behavior. Check the row/column indexing matches the frozen whitening representation before capture. Do NOT execute ConditionC0QualificationSuite: its ordinary tests run paired DEV studies. Compiling that existing suite suffices for the test-helper scope; execute only the new trace suite.

## Trace design

`ShapeObjective` is already public and contains the five callbacks needed for a
test wrapper. Build a test-local `TraceObjective(delegate, counters)` that
implements it by exactly one delegate call per callback:

- `scoreNode(node)` records node and returned scalar;
- `jetAtNode(node, out)`, `jetAt(coordinates, out)`, and
  `energyAt(coordinates, out)` record operation, copied coordinates where
  applicable, returned value/Boolean, and copied finite/nonfinite jet fields;
- `grid` and `amplitudeCount` are direct delegation and are not events.

The wrapper also snapshots the passed `DecoderCounters` before and after each
callback. It may copy scalar/array values for logging; it must make no callback
for logging, mutation, or verification. Events need an ordinal and must be
serialized deterministically as JSON lines (hexadecimal Double text is
preferred for values). The raw sbt output is the trace receipt; do not add a
runtime file writer.

A wrapper cannot observe `ShapeDecoder`'s private `current`, `value`,
`accepted`, `scale`, or comparison predicate. The report must label callback
sequence interpretations as **inferred**, never direct branch observations.
Direct observations are the callbacks, returned energy/jet values, coordinates,
and counter snapshots only.

Because `CompactConditionRuntime` owns a private decoder, do not try to inject
the wrapper through it. The factory/test must project the literal response,
call `objective.pointAt(z, e)`, then construct `new ShapeDecoder` directly with
the same candidate policy/no-prior/noise variance. This is feasible with the
existing public `CompactConditionObjective`, `ShapeObjective`, and
`CompactConditionPreparation.project` APIs. It is a test-only decode of one
literal column.

## Required tests and receipts

The new suite must perform, on each platform:

1. an unwrapped direct decode of the literal column;
2. a wrapped direct decode of a fresh but equivalent objective and fresh
   counters;
3. exact equality of status, budget exit, node, coordinates, energy, amplitudes,
   Hessians, conditional SD, ambiguity gap, and every `DecoderCounters` field
   between the wrapped and unwrapped runs on that platform;
4. a nonempty, finite-or-explicitly-nonfinite callback trace whose callback
   count agrees with the matching counter deltas. The wrapper must not increase
   objective callback/counter work.

Print one self-identifying JSON trace line for each platform run, including
fixture digest, source freeze, policy label, direct terminal result, all
callback events, and direct versus wrapped comparison. Do not assert identical
terminal results between JVM and JS: the purpose is to reveal that difference
on identical literal input. The document must compare the actual platform
traces after both runs, list the first divergent direct callback if one exists,
or state that branch divergence remains unobserved if all callback values agree.

Use independently parsed JSON (`python3 -c` is sufficient) to validate every
printed trace line from both raw logs and to compare the two platform records.
Record the parser command, its actual exit status, count of trace lines, and
whether it found a first direct divergence. The parser must not recalculate or
fit any objective.

## Required execution

Before editing, normal Mote preflight/begin must reserve only the four paths.
Freeze source while the shared job is queued or running. Use the shared lock:

```text
python3 /private/tmp/scalafim-execution-20260929/run-sbt.py \
  /private/tmp/scalafim-execution-20260929/c0-platform-trace \
  c0-platform-trace-final.log \
  'firstLevelLawsJVM/testOnly scalafim.fmri.laws.profile.ConditionC0PlatformTraceSuite' \
  'firstLevelLawsJS/testOnly scalafim.fmri.laws.profile.ConditionC0PlatformTraceSuite'
```

This is one bounded literal-column diagnostic, not an invitation to execute
other C0 suites, a cohort, or a compile-all. Preserve raw log, metadata, parser
output, source/fixture hashes, JVM/JS provider/runtime/classpath closure, and
complete trace comparison in the owned verification document. A clean actual
exit and nonzero test count on both targets are required. If test naming or
Scala.js output routing prevents capture of trace lines, stop and report that
concrete blocker rather than adding a production trace API.

After actual success, commit only the four owned paths with canonical local
identity. No push, ticket closure, or scientific/performance qualification.
Hand the child back to the parent with explicit reservation release and exact
SHA, raw/meta hashes, fixture digest, parser evidence, and the remaining causal
uncertainty.

## Success boundary

Success is a reproducible, no-extra-work trace of the frozen literal response
on both platforms. It can confirm an earlier arithmetic difference, or narrow
the difference to an unobservable decoder comparison. It does not authorize a
comparison tolerance, decoder repair, altered C0 gate, fresh stream, or any
scientific conclusion.
set.title: Trace identical literal C0 response across JVM and Scala.js without policy changes
